newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wharf says no decision on court appeal.
newsitem.headline: Wharf says no decision on court appeal.

text.p: Wharf (Holdings) Ltd said on Tuesday it had not decided whether to appeal against a decision by a Hong Kong court to award about HK$225 million plus interest to a Danish financing institution in March.
"We are waiting for legal advice as to which step we should take later on....It is not finalised," said Gary Shing, head of corporate affairs at Wheelock and Co Ltd and Wharf.

Wharf said last month that a Danish financing institution, ADS, had been awarded about HK$225 million plus interest due to omissions by a former director of Wheelock Marden & Co to supply certain information to ADS. It said at the time that Wheelock Marden was considering the judgment with its legal advisers.
Wharf took over Wheelock Marden in the mid-1980's. Both unlisted Wheelock Marden and listed Wharf (Holdings) are subsidiaries of Wheelock and Co.
The South China Morning Post reported on Tuesday that Wharf could face HK$1 billion in potential damages payments from legal action against the group in Hong Kong and the United States.
Shing declined to comment on the report but said the claims had been detailed in both Wheelock and Wharf's annual reports.

"Claims for damages plus interest aggregating approximately HK$902.6 million have been brought by a third party against inter alia a subsidiary as a consequence of financing commitments previously entered into by its former subsidiaries," Wheelock said in its annual report for the year ended in March 1996.
"Taking into account the advice received from legal advisors, the management is of the opnion that there are reasonable grounds to resist the claims," it added.
The South China Morning Post also said that Wharf was embroiled in a trial in the U.S. city of Denver where a cable television management company was suing Wharf for about US$70 million in damages.
"It is still going on...We have no comment at this point," said Shing.
